claims.text: Flydubai temporarily suspended flights to and from Israel following an attack on a pilot.
On September 30, 2026, Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv transmitted emergency signals and made a sharp descent of more than 17,000 feet from 34,000 feet.
Flydubai flight FZ1073 diverted to Prince Sultan Bin Abdel Aziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, while carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children.
Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed inside the cockpit by his co-pilot during an alleged attempt to crash the Flydubai aircraft.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Captain Smit Machchhar a hero and stated that India is proud of him.
President Droupadi Murmu commended Captain Smit Machchhar on X for his bravery and quick response in preventing a major tragedy.
Despite sustaining severe injuries, Captain Smit Machchhar activated the cockpit door release switch to allow crew and passengers to intervene and overpower the attacker.
Two off-duty Flydubai pilots travelling as passengers stepped in to assist in overpowering the attacker and diverting the aircraft.
Captain Smit Machchhar is a 50-year-old Mumbai native who spent 11 years with SpiceJet before joining Flydubai in 2022.
Before joining Flydubai, Captain Smit Machchhar logged nearly 9,750 flying hours over a 15-year career primarily flying Boeing 737 aircraft.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Captain Smit Machchhar a true hero.
Airline SpiceJet praised Flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, stating that all of India is proud.
According to Israeli officials, the co-pilot accused of stabbing Captain Smit Machchhar is an Omani citizen.
Passenger Yaniv Hayoun stated that he placed the attacker in a chokehold and dragged him out after catching him attempting to destroy instrument panels.
The Israeli embassy in Australia confirmed that a Jewish couple from Sydney was on board the diverted Flydubai flight.
Israel's ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman stated that the cockpit attack was an attempt to hit at the peace established by the Abraham Accords.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi asked who at the Election Commission ordered Tata Consultancy Services to illegally alter the online Form 6 voter registration form on the ECINET portal.
Tata Consultancy Services handles the core digital backend infrastructure and ECINET portal management for the Election Commission of India.
An investigative report by The Indian Express revealed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections to changes made to the online Form 6 on the ECINET portal.
The Election Commission removed the additional Special Intensive Revision declaration from Form 6 on its ECINET portal for states where the revision process concluded, effective September 30, 2026.
The additional Special Intensive Revision declaration attached to Form 6 remains available on the Election Commission portal for 13 states where the voter revision exercise is ongoing.
INDIA bloc leaders announced a Save Democracy March from October 2 to October 8, a protest march to the Election Commission on October 6, and a planned meeting with President Droupadi Murmu.
The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh will hold its Akhil Bharatiya Karyakari Mandal executive council meeting in Indore starting November 2, 2026.
The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh is restructuring its organisation by replacing prant pracharaks with sambhag pracharaks, increasing the number of pracharaks from 46 to 85.
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh outreach head Sunil Ambekar stated that if wrong people are found on electoral lists, there should be a legally sound policy to rectify anomalies.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh cited former Chief Election Commissioner O. P. Rawat as stating that nearly 14 crore voters had been disenfranchised through the Special Intensive Revision.
Former CEC O. P. Rawat stated that the Election Commission has lost credibility and that Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi should have done more to oppose improper decisions.
Leaders from 19 opposition parties in the INDIA bloc called for future elections in India to be conducted using paper ballots.

Odisha's Chief Electoral Officer R. S. Gopalan applied for voluntary retirement from service on September 30, 2026, citing personal reasons after the Special Intensive Revision process concluded in the state.
Speaking at an IGNCA event on September 30, 2026, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh publicity in-charge Sunil Ambekar called for a nationwide National Register of Citizens.
AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that the Special Intensive Revision exercise was a backdoor National Register of Citizens.
